# Movement

Movement has its own turn budget. Every foot traveled through Difficult Terrain costs one extra foot.

- Check visible obstacles, occupied spaces, terrain, and reach before relying on a destination.
- Moving into contact, holding a chokepoint, maintaining separation, and withdrawing serve different purposes; name the purpose that supports the shared objective.
- Leaving the reach of a creature that can see the mover can trigger an Opportunity Attack. Disengage can prevent that consequence for the rest of the current turn.
- Do not assume that the shortest-looking route is open or that a destination visible on the board is reachable this turn.

Use the tabletop's gutter label only when an exact destination matters; otherwise express the intended relationship to a visible creature or object.
